transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this. It's, well, it's probably just a silly quirk, really, and I hate to even take up your time with it. 

But I work in retail, and... well, what brings me in is that, if I'm in the back stockroom and I even just think there might be a bat, or, you know, something flapping around up near the ceiling... my heart just immediately jumps. I start sweating a bit, and I just get this sudden feeling like I need to get out of there right that second. 

I know it sounds a little ridiculous for a grown man to get so worked up over nothing, but... does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you usually help people with?
When you're not at work or not in the stockroom, do you also feel that kind of sudden fear or anxiety when you think about or encounter other specific things or situations?

No, no, not really. I mean, it's just the bats, honestly. If I'm out walking the dog or just, you know, going about my day, I'm totally fine. I don't really get that feeling with anything else. 

I guess I'm pretty normal otherwise, you know? It's just that one specific thing. I hope that's okay, that I don't have a whole list of things to tell you about. Is it normal for it to just be one thing like that?
When you're in the stockroom and you think there might be a bat, do you ever feel like you need to escape or have trouble leaving the area, or maybe feel trapped even if you could leave?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I feel trapped, exactly. I mean, I know I *can* leave. But... well, I do try to avoid being in that situation in the first place, if I'm being completely honest. 

I don't want to make a big deal out of it, but I've actually been... well, swapping out my closing shifts when I can. Just so I don't have to be back there alone at night. And, um, I'll take the long way around the loading dock just to avoid walking near the darker corners. 

When I absolutely have to go back there, like if I have to check the back stairwell... I just make myself do it as fast as humanly possible. I'll hold my phone out with the flashlight on, and I just... I feel so on edge the whole time, just waiting for something to swoop down. 

I know it's silly to go to all that trouble, and I hope it doesn't make me sound like a terrible employee. I still get my work done, I promise! I just... I try to work around it, you know? Is that... is that a common way people handle this sort of thing?
